fullPassage: Anthropologist Gregory Bateson suggests that we tend to understand the world by focusing in on particular features within it. Take platypuses. We might zoom in so closely to their fur that each hair appears different. We might also zoom out to the extent where it appears as a single, uniform object. We might take the platypus as an individual, or we might treat it as part of a larger unit such as a species or an ecosystem. It's possible to move between many of these perspectives, although we may need some additional tools and skills to zoom in on individual pieces of hair or zoom out to entire ecosystems. Crucially, however, we can only take up one perspective at a time. We can pay attention to the varied behavior of individual animals, look at what unites them into a single species, or look at them as part of bigger ecological patterns. Every possible perspective involves emphasizing certain aspects and ignoring others.

det.korean: ① such → so. 뒤에 부사 closely가 오므로 so(so + 부사/형용사 ... that).
det.analysis:
❌ ① such → so: 뒤에 부사 closely가 왔어요. 'so + 형용사/부사 + that(너무 ~해서 …하다)' 구문이므로 so가 맞아요. such는 뒤에 명사가 올 때 써요 ←정답
✅ ② their: 뒤 명사 fur를 꾸미는 소유격 ←맞음
✅ ③ where: 앞의 the extent(정도)를 받는 관계부사 ←맞음
✅ ④ such as: '~와 같은'의 표현 ←맞음
det.tip: so + 부사/형용사 + that vs such + 명사

✅ ① to step back and view things at the broadest scale(한 발 물러서 가장 넓은 규모로 보다): 비유의 뜻과 일치 ←정답
❌ ② to travel across many different natural environments(여러 자연환경을 여행하다): 물리적 이동이 아님
❌ ③ to destroy the smaller parts of an ecosystem(생태계의 작은 부분을 파괴하다): 본문에 없음
❌ ④ to count all the species living in one area(한 지역의 모든 종을 세다): 세는 행위가 아님
det.tip: zoom out = 관점을 넓혀 크게 보기(비유)

questions.passage: Anthropologist Gregory Bateson suggests that we tend to understand the world by focusing in on particular features within it. Take platypuses. We might zoom in so closely to their fur that each hair appears different. We might also zoom out to the extent where it appears as a single, uniform object. We might take the platypus as an individual, or we might treat it as part of a larger unit such as a species or an ecosystem. It's possible to move between many of these perspectives, although we may need some additional tools and skills to zoom in on individual pieces of hair or zoom out to entire ecosystems. Crucially, however, we can only take up one perspective at a time. We can pay attention to the varied behavior of individual animals, look at what unites them into a single species, or look at them as part of bigger ecological patterns. Every possible perspective involves emphasizing certain aspects and ignoring <u>others</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 others가 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: others = (강조되지 않은) 다른 측면들.
det.analysis:
밑줄 친 others는 앞의 emphasizing certain aspects(특정 측면을 강조)와 짝을 이뤄요. 강조하는 '특정 측면(certain aspects)'이 있으면, 무시되는 것은 '나머지 측면들(other aspects)'이에요.

❌ ① 다른 관점들: aspects(측면)를 가리킴, 관점 아님
❌ ② 다른 동물들: 문맥과 무관
❌ ③ 다른 생태계들: 문맥과 무관
✅ ④ 강조되지 않은 다른 측면들: certain aspects의 나머지 aspects ←정답
det.tip: certain aspects ↔ others(= other aspects)

det.korean: 빈칸: 하나의 균일한 대상(a single, uniform object).
det.analysis:
❌ ① a completely different creature(완전히 다른 생물): 축소해서 보는 것과 무관
✅ ② a single, uniform object: 아주 멀리 축소하면(zoom out) 전체가 '하나의 균일한 대상'처럼 보임 ←정답

❌ ④ an unfamiliar new pattern(낯선 새 패턴): 문맥 불일치

det.korean: closely (가까이).
